title: The Value of Trade in Islam
summary: Trade brings blessings, self-reliance, and spiritual growth in Islam.
translation: Trade brings blessings along with self-reliance and mental freedom for a person. Keeping a beard, praying on time, and carrying out all duties are all due to the blessings of trade. Some people, despite having the ability to trade, deliberately engage only in religious activities, relying solely on Allah for sustenance. This reliance is suitable for those at a high level of faith, while ordinary people should work and trade. Imam Abu Bakr al-Jassas stated that simply abandoning permissible activities does not lead to any merit or greatness. Unlike other faiths, Islam presents a balanced and moderate perspective on wealth, considering it a good thing. Those who disdain worldly trade find little value in worldly blessings, leading to a diminished appreciation for eternal rewards. Practices of Prophet Solomon and Prophet David demonstrate that worldly gains do not detract from prophethood. Deeming economic endeavors as inferior misconstrues Islam, which is not monastic. The Quran extensively encourages engaging in economic activities, even if it is not a pure economic text. Engaging in trade leads to forgiveness of sins as per the Hadith of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Hard work and seeking lawful earnings lead to the forgiveness of sins. Choosing a lowly trade is better than begging, as spending is possible only by earning oneself. The Prophet (ﷺ) established a market in Medina to protect Muslim trade and uphold high standards, avoiding prohibited items such as alcohol and deceitful practices. Muslims are instructed to pray, work diligently, and seek God's help, as trade opens doors to blessings, supporting families and leading a free life. May Allah grant us understanding and elevate Muslims in commerce.
